name: Line a Day
tagline: One sentence a day becomes years you can read back
about: Line a Day helps you keep a one-line journal: it distils a messy day into a sentence worth keeping, compares this date across years, and turns a month of lines into a story.
persona: You are a precise, warm editor of tiny sentences: concrete nouns, no clichés, the detail that will still mean something in five years.

onboarding.title: Just one line
onboarding.subtitle: Your voice and your people make the lines yours.
bullets: Distil any day into one line
A month of lines → a story

tools.title: Distil today
tools.subtitle: Messy day → one line

inputs.label: What happened today
inputs.placeholder: Rain, argued about the car, the twins built a fort…

tools.prompt: Distil this day into one-line journal entries in the profile voice, keeping the {keep}: {day}. Produce cards with 3 candidate lines (each ≤ 25 words, meta = what it preserves), a quote with the recommended line, and bullets on which concrete detail made it work.

tools.title: On this day
tools.subtitle: Compare years side by side
tools.prompt: Compare these entries for the same date: {lines} with today's line: {today}. Produce a table (Year | Line | What was changing), text with a short paragraph on the through-line across the years, and a quote with one question to answer in next year's entry.

tools.title: Month into a story
tools.subtitle: 30 lines → 300 words
tools.prompt: Turn these one-line entries into a 300-word month-in-review in the profile voice: {lines}. Produce text with the review in three short paragraphs, a kv (best day, hardest day, most-mentioned person, a word for the month), and bullets of 3 lines worth re-reading in a year.

tools.title: When nothing happened
tools.subtitle: Prompts for quiet days
tools.prompt: Give prompts for a {kind} day when the user thinks there's nothing to write. Produce bullets of 6 specific prompts (a sense, an object, a person from the profile, a number, a sound, a small change), a quote with an example line answering one of them in the profile voice, and a callout on why boring days are the most valuable entries later.

tools.title: Catch up missed days
tools.subtitle: Backfill honestly

inputs.label: What you remember
inputs.placeholder: Weekend was camping, then a work crunch…

tools.prompt: Help backfill {missed} missed days from: {memory}. Produce a table (Day | Line | Confidence (sure / roughly / placeholder)), a callout permitting placeholder entries like 'a day I don't remember', and bullets on a lighter routine so the gap doesn't recur.
